title: Build the mutation journal and kondo trash
why: ADR-0001 makes every mutation reversible, and nothing in the app writes yet. The journal and trash have to exist before the first toggle, not alongside it.
what: Append-before-write journal at <kondo-data>/journal.jsonl, a kondo-owned trash at <kondo-data>/trash/<journal-id>/, and an undo(journalId) workspace method. Ships with the ADR-0001 safety-invariant tests docs/testing.md defers to the first mutation: journal written before the store is touched, undo restores a fixture byte-for-byte, no write lands outside a known store.
notes:
2026-08-29 unverified: launch the app (npm run dev) and confirm the composition root resolves <kondo-data> to Electron userData (%APPDATA%/Kondo on Windows) rather than anything under ~/.claude. electron/main/index.ts now passes app.getPath(userData) into createLocator, and no test can construct the real Electron app, so this one line is proven only by types. Nothing is visible in the UI yet: check the resolved path, not a screen.
2026-08-29 Shipped electron/main/workspace/mutations.ts. mutate() appends one JSON line to <kondo-data>/journal.jsonl and fsyncs it before any store byte moves, then runs the move/trash/write steps; a step names a store root plus a relative path and pathWithin refuses anything that escapes. Trash displaces into <kondo-data>/trash/<journal-id>/<store>/<relative>, never an unlink; the EXDEV fallback is copy, verify, then release. undo() reverses a whole multi-step operation in reverse order, is itself journaled with an undoOf link, and moves current bytes into its own trash before restoring displaced ones. Locator gained kondoDataRoot from Electron userData with KONDO_DATA_ROOT for fixtures. Seam gained journalList, journalUndo and trashSize plus JournalEntryInfo and TrashReport; no mutation channel ships, per the plan. Red-green proof: test/mutation.test.ts failed on a missing module before the code existed, went 12/12 green after, and swapping appendJournal/act inside mutate() turned 2 of the 12 red again (the ordering case and the failed-journal-write case); the swap was reverted. Checks run: npm run typecheck exits 0; npm run lint exits 0 (oxlint 1.80.0, confirmed live by a deliberate probe file that it did flag, then deleted); npm test 55/55 across 11 files; node .jig/checks/run.mjs reports no findings. Beyond the stated file surface I also updated docs/testing.md (its safety-invariant bullet still said these tests were deferred to the first mutation), docs/plans/001 (status plus a What actually shipped table of 4 divergences), docs/plans/README.md and CHANGELOG.md, because AGENTS.md treats a PR that leaves a doc wrong as incomplete. docs/adr/ needed no change: ADR-0001 already states this design, so no ADR was invented. Work is on branch worktree-foreman-001-mutation-journal in .claude/worktrees/foreman-001-mutation-journal. Two PostToolUse jig hook firings were false positives, quoting the src/ renderer rule and the test/ real-store rule at files under electron/ and test/; the same checks through the real driver report no findings.

title: Introduce the kind registry and capability matrix
why: foundations.md names this as v0.2's structural step. A single boolean write-permission model was enough for skills alone and does not survive five entity kinds.
what: Replace the hard-coded adapter set with kinds that each supply discover, read, capabilities, enable and disable, with identity per ADR-0008. Write permission becomes a capability matrix keyed by kind, scope and operation rather than one flag. The snapshot cache, error isolation and id allow-list skeleton stay as they are.
notes:
2026-08-29 2026-08-29 Discrepancy with the brief: there was no single write-permission boolean to replace. Grepping writable/read-only/canWrite/permission/mutable across electron, shared, src and test returned only unrelated hits (`readonly` modifiers in mutations.ts and scan.ts, the string 'read-only preview' in src/app/app.tsx). SkillInfo.enabled is a state flag carried from Claude's own convention (ADR-0006), not a permission flag, and it stays as it was. The matrix is therefore introduced fresh rather than replacing a flag; nothing was removed. 2026-08-29 Shipped two new modules. electron/main/workspace/capabilities.ts holds the matrix: MATRIX is Record<EntityKind, Record<scope, Capabilities>> and capabilitiesFor(kind, scope) returns the row, with an unrecognized scope refusing both operations rather than throwing (ADR-0005). Rows encode Claude's own conventions per ADR-0006 - a user skill may be disabled and a user-disabled one enabled, a plugin-shipped skill neither, plugins toggle in any settings layer, and hooks refuse both because Claude has no per-hook disable convention. electron/main/workspace/kinds.ts holds the registry: seven entries (skill, plugin, hook, settings, project, session, desktopSession) each supplying discover, read, capabilities, enable and disable, plus createKindContext which memoizes the settings-layer and plugin-manifest reads per call. Code and desktop sessions are two entries sharing kind 'session' because they live in different stores; the matrix keys them apart by scope. enable/disable are seats returning null on every kind - the matrix says what is permitted, and no MutationPlan is built and no channel invokes one, per this entry's no-new-mutation-path rule. 2026-08-29 Invariants held. workspace.ts now names no adapter: grepping scanSkills|scanPlugins|hooksFromLayers|readSettingsLayers|desktopSessions|toSessionProjects|toSessionSummaries|summarizeTranscript across workspace.ts, ipc.ts and index.ts returns only the KondoApi method name desktopSessions, never the adapter. Every id-shape guard, badRequest and unknownId path in workspace.ts is byte-identical to before; only the line that picked an adapter changed. The lazy context preserves today's exact I/O and collector ordering - hooksList still reads only the settings layers, skillsList still reads projects then layers then the plugin manifest then the skill trees - which is why the read-path, boundary (ADR-0002) and mutation (ADR-0001) suites pass untouched. 2026-08-29 Seam: shared/contract.ts gained EntityKind, CapabilityOperation, CapabilityDecision, Capabilities and EntityIdentity, and SessionProject, SessionSummary, DesktopSession, SkillInfo, PluginInfo, HookInfo and SettingsLayerInfo now extend EntityIdentity, so every entity crosses the bridge carrying its kind and its matrix row. Each adapter stamps them where it builds the row, so the renderer never parses an id to learn what it may do. No new channel and no preload change: JournalEntryInfo.kind and MutationPlan.kind were tightened from string to EntityKind now that the vocabulary is defined. 2026-08-29 Red-green proof: flipping MATRIX skill/user/disable from ALLOW to a denial turned test/kinds.test.ts red at the 'keys permission on kind, scope and operation' assertion (1 failed, 8 passed); reverting returned it to 9/9. 2026-08-29 Checks run: npm run typecheck exits 0 (also with --force, a full rebuild); npm run lint exits 0 (oxlint 1.80.0, silent); npm test 64/64 across 12 files, up from 55/11, with every pre-existing test unchanged; node .jig/checks/run.mjs reports no findings. Two PostToolUse jig hook firings were false positives, quoting the raw-path-across-the-seam guard at electron/main/workspace/workspace.ts and the renderer-purity guard at test/kinds.test.ts - both guards are scoped to electron/preload, electron/main/ipc.ts and src/ respectively, and the real driver reports nothing. 2026-08-29 Scope drift - predicted and touched: electron/main/workspace/, shared/contract.ts, docs/foundations.md; touched but unpredicted: test/kinds.test.ts and CHANGELOG.md. The test file is this task's own coverage (docs/testing.md requires adapter-level tests and AGENTS.md makes all three checks a completion bar); the changelog bullet is required by docs/README.md, which treats a PR that leaves a doc wrong as incomplete. No docs/plans/ file was written: docs/plans/README.md says a plan is the first commit of a feature, not a document written afterwards. 2026-08-29 Work is on branch foreman/002-kind-registry-and-capability-matrix, created from main; there is no git remote on this repo.

title: Enable and disable skills through the native convention
why: ADR-0006: kondo speaks Claude's own language rather than keeping shadow state. Disabling a skill means moving it to skills.disabled, which Claude already honours.
what: Move a user-scope skill between ~/.claude/skills and ~/.claude/skills.disabled through the journal, with the scoped equivalent for project skills. Plugin-shipped skills are read-only and the capability matrix must say so. The UI gets a toggle per skill row that re-reads the store after every mutation.
notes:
2026-08-29 unverified: run npm run dev, open the Skills tab, and look at the new toggle column. Check that a global skill shows a Disable button that flips the row to the disabled pill after one click without a manual refresh, that a plugin-shipped skill shows a greyed-out Enable whose tooltip reads the matrix reason (Plugin-shipped skills follow their plugin - toggle the plugin instead), and that a refusal renders as the red card above the table. Every one of these is proven headlessly in test/skill-toggle.test.ts; what no command can settle is how the button reads and whether the list visibly re-reads rather than flickering.
2026-08-29 Shipped kondo's first user-facing mutation. A skill toggle is one journaled move step between skills and skills.disabled in the skill's own scope; no second write path exists and nothing is unlinked. kinds.ts gained skillPlacement/skillPlan, replacing the skill entry's noPlanYet seat: the plan is built only when entity.capabilities[operation].allowed, so the matrix from 002 is the gate and a refused operation never reaches a MutationPlan. workspace.skillToggle validates the id shape and the operation, resolves the skill through kinds.skill.read, and on a null plan pushes the matrix's own reason as a new not-permitted ScanError rather than inventing prose. Seam additions: skillToggle(skillId, operation) plus its channel, ScanErrorCode not-permitted, SkillScope project-disabled. No new per-skill capability field was needed - see discrepancy 1. THREE DISCREPANCIES WITH THE BRIEF. (1) The brief asked to extend shared/contract.ts with 'the per-skill capability the renderer needs to render its toggle state'; entry 002 already ships it - SkillInfo extends EntityIdentity, which carries capabilities - so nothing was added for it and skills.tsx reads that existing field. (2) docs/plans/001 divergence 3 states project roots arrive with entry 005, and mutations.ts indeed knew only user and desktop. 003 cannot toggle a project skill without one, so createMutations gained an optional extraRoot resolver and resolveIn/rootOf became async; createWorkspace supplies project:<dirName> from its verified-project cache, resolving to <project>/.claude so ADR-0002 confinement is the store boundary itself. The ADR-0001 decision-6 containment check is applied to dynamically resolved roots too. (3) scanSkills had no project-disabled scope, so disabling a project skill would have made it vanish from the list with no way to re-enable it. Added the scope to SkillScope, a matrix row, and a scan of <project>/.claude/skills.disabled. RED-GREEN PROOF, three separate runs, each reverted: swapping appendJournal and act inside mutate() turned 'appends the journal entry before the skill directory moves' red (expected 4 to be less than 0); flipping MATRIX skill/plugin from neither(PLUGIN_OWNED) to ALLOW turned the plugin-refusal test red; misrouting skillPlacement's project case to the user store turned both project-scope tests red. CHECKS RUN: npm run typecheck exits 0 (also npx tsc -b --force, a full rebuild); npm run lint exits 0 (oxlint, silent); npm test 73/73 across 13 files, up from 64/12, every pre-existing test passing unchanged; node .jig/checks/run.mjs reports no findings. test/skill-toggle.test.ts holds 9 cases: user disable lands in skills.disabled and nowhere else with an empty trash, user enable, undo restores the tree byte-for-byte, a project skill toggles both ways inside its own .claude while the user store's hash is unchanged, a write-boundary sweep over the project toggle, the plugin refusal in both directions with no journal entry, the already-enabled refusal, journal-before-move ordering, and refusals for a free-form path, an unknown id and an unknown operation. Both project cases ran (tmpdir has no hyphen); they self-skip on a hyphenated tmpdir like boundary.test.ts. hashTree, exists and recordWrites moved from test/mutation.test.ts into test/helpers.ts so both suites share one write-path probe; mutation.test.ts's 12 cases are otherwise untouched. SCOPE DRIFT beyond the stated surface: CHANGELOG.md, docs/domain.md and docs/testing.md. docs/README.md makes a PR that leaves a doc wrong incomplete; domain.md gained the project-scope skills.disabled convention with a diamond (expected) marker, honestly noting it is unobserved in the wild and written because ADR-0006 chose the scoped equivalent. No docs/plans/ file was written - docs/plans/README.md says a plan is a feature's first commit, not a document written afterwards. One PostToolUse jig firing was a false positive, quoting the raw-path-across-the-seam guard at test/skill-toggle.test.ts (the test that proves a path IS refused); the real driver reports nothing. Work is on branch foreman/003-enable-disable-skills, created from main; this repo has no git remote.

title: Enable and disable plugins per scope
why: A plugin's enabled state lives in enabledPlugins in a settings layer, and today kondo only reports which layers list it. Toggling by hand means editing JSON in the right file.
what: Edit enabledPlugins in the chosen settings layer through the journal, preserving formatting and unrelated keys. The plugins view gains a per-scope toggle showing which layer wins. A layer that does not exist yet is created only on explicit confirmation.

title: Move a skill between scopes and projects
why: Skills accumulate in the wrong scope and moving one by hand means copying a directory and hoping nothing referenced the old path. This is the feature the tool is named for.
what: Copy, verify, then trash the source, all journaled as one reversible operation. Handles user to project, project to user, and project to project. Refuses a move whose destination already holds that skill name rather than merging, and refuses plugin-owned sources outright.

title: Add the tidy sweep with a dry-run preview
why: A store with 8,921 project directories accumulates stale sessions, empty transcripts and dead caches that nobody will clear by hand. Reclaiming that space is why staleness is measured at all.
what: Bulk-archive stale sessions, sweep empty transcripts and orphaned sidecars, and clear reclaimable cache directories, each through the trash. Every sweep shows a dry-run preview naming counts and bytes before anything moves, and the whole sweep is one journal entry so undo restores it together.

title: Surface undo and the trash in the UI
why: ADR-0001 makes undo a first-class feature, so it needs a first-class surface. Trashed transcripts persist until emptied, and SECURITY.md requires the size to be visible.
what: A view listing journal entries newest first, each with what it did and an undo action, plus trash size and an explicit empty-trash action that is never bundled into another operation. Emptying is the one destructive act kondo has and must read like it.

title: Register jig session guards in .claude/settings.json
why: The four jig guards are armed in .jig/config.json but nothing invokes the runner on PostToolUse, so they fire only in CI and npm run guards, never live while a session edits.
what: Add a PostToolUse hook on Edit and Write that calls jig hooks/runner.js. The obstacle is the path: the runner sits at a version-pinned plugin cache path, so committing it breaks other machines and every plugin upgrade. Solve that first with a repo-local shim, a settings.local.json entry, or a resolver, then wire it. Confirm the guards deny live afterwards.
